1.0.0.en: "The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah:" [1].

1.0.1.en: This statement is regarded as an introduction to the whole book, which contains a collection of visions and prophecies revealed to Isaiah in various circumstances: in the days of Uzziah the Great, Jotham the good king, Ahaz with his dark reign, Hezekiah and Manasseh, and so on... Yet he calls them all a "vision," because although they are different visions, they represent one unity, with one goal: God's declaration of His thought, His will and His plan of salvation, for the building up of the holy congregation, or for the sanctification of mankind who believe in Him.

1.0.2.en: The visions here are not dreams that the prophet enjoyed during his sleep, but divine revelations presented to the prophet while he was awake, while his senses were still because of their limitation and inability, so that the prophet may say with St. John the Seer: "I was in the Spirit" (Rev 1:10). Perhaps by "vision" is meant the divine inspiration proper to prophecy.

1.0.3.en: These visions are "concerning Judah and Jerusalem," that is, they concern the kingdom of Judah or the southern kingdom (Judah and Benjamin), and they focus on the capital, Jerusalem, as the city of God in which is His holy temple; but they also included prophecies about the northern kingdom (the rest of the tribes) and about the neighboring kingdoms that had a relationship with the people.

1.0.4.en: These visions are the word of God, which does not touch Judah in the eighth century B.C. alone, but touches the life of every person who longs for the salvation of his soul and for enjoying fellowship with God, as it is written in the Book of Deuteronomy: "The LORD our God made a covenant with us in Horeb. The LORD made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day" (Deut 5:2-3)... It is God's word and His declarations to every human soul!

1.1.0.en: "Hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth: for the LORD hath spoken, I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" [2].

1.1.1.en: The book begins with a great trial whose two parties are God and man, in which lifeless nature, heaven and earth, is summoned to witness this trial.

1.1.2.en: Perhaps the prophet Isaiah summoned nature as the prophet Moses had done before: "Give ear, O ye heavens, and I will speak; and hear, O earth, the words of my mouth" (Deut 32:1). It is as though Isaiah were assuring his people that what he utters is an extension of the words of the prophet Moses, in whom every Jew takes pride. Perhaps he wanted to stress how hard man's heart is and how blind his insight, and therefore he summons lifeless nature to bear witness against him, a matter that his contemporary, the prophet Micah, made clear: "Hear ye, O mountains, the LORD'S controversy, and ye strong foundations of the earth: for the LORD hath a controversy with his people" (Mic 6:2).

1.1.3.en: Perhaps this summons was made by an angel on behalf of the Lord, to bear witness against man in the hardness of his heart. Or perhaps the Lord Himself made this summons, since He did not summon His holy temple or His Law to testify against them, but asked for lifeless nature, which fulfilled God's purposes and accomplished its mission by submitting to Him, while man became utterly corrupt because of his disobedience.

1.1.4.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [It is now fitting to summon heaven (as witness), since there is no man who hears and bears witness to these things.]

1.1.5.en: St. Clement of Alexandria sees that God summons the Gnostics, that is, the believers who possess heavenly divine knowledge (heaven), just as He summons those whose hearts are occupied with temporal and earthly things.

1.1.6.en: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" [2].

1.1.7.en: God does not bear human feelings, yet He is not a lifeless being; rather, He is "Love" itself, unique in His love for His heavenly and earthly creation, especially His love toward man. Therefore, when He speaks with us human beings, He speaks to us in our human language, expressing His love as though with human feelings, so that we may touch Him and experience union and fellowship with Him.

1.1.8.en: God knows that nothing can grieve a man and make him lose the taste of life like the feeling that he has failed in raising his children, especially if they rise up against him declaring rebellion against him. With the vast difference, God reveals His feelings toward fallen man: he is a beloved son, to whom his heavenly Father offers every possibility of a transcendent life, but he meets love with rebellion.

1.1.9.en: He called His people "My firstborn son" (Ex 4:22), and so He calls us His children, for we did not receive the spirit of bondage but the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father (Rom 8:15).

1.1.10.en: God expects us to bear the spirit of sonship that responds to God's unique, tender fatherhood, which cost Him much, offering His only-begotten Son as a sacrifice to acquire us for Himself as children in the waters of Baptism. St. Gregory the Theologian says: [Like a good shepherd You sought after the lost one; like a true father You labored with me who had fallen.]

1.1.11.en: St. Cyprian speaks to us about our duty as children of God toward their Father, saying: [If we are children of God, if we have indeed begun to be His temples, if we receive His Holy Spirit, we must live in holiness and spirituality.]

1.1.12.en: God reproaches His children for their rebellion, for the rebellion of sons is more bitter than the rebellion of hired servants and slaves, and the wounds of loved ones, especially sons, are harsher than those caused by enemies.

1.1.13.en: St. Irenaeus sees that God created man as His son who imitates Him and fulfills His divine will toward him, but when he glorifies God and accepts the counsel of the enemy of good, he becomes a son of the devil. For this reason the Lord Christ called those who opposed Him "sons of the devil" (Jn 8:44), and denied that they had a spiritual descent from Abraham (Jn 8:39).

1.1.14.en: * According to nature, that is, by creation, we are said to be sons of God, since we are all His creation. But as regards obedience and teaching, we are not all sons of God; only those who believe in Him and fulfill His will are (sons). Those who do not believe and do not obey His will are the sons of Satan and his angels, because they do the works of Satan.

1.1.15.en: St. Irenaeus * When the Pharisees persecuted our Lord and Savior, He wept because of their coming destruction. They mistreated Him, but He did not repay them in kind, nor even with a threat; even when they treated Him with contempt and killed Him, He on the contrary grieved over their audacity... All these things were before their eyes in the Holy Scriptures, for the Psalmist prophesied, saying: "Strange children have worked vanity against me" (Ps 18:45). And Isaiah said: "I have nourished and brought up children, and they have rebelled against me" (Isa 1:2). They were no longer the people of God or a holy nation, but became the rulers of Sodom and the people of Gomorrah (Isa 1:10). They exceeded the sin of the people of Sodom, as the prophet prophesied: [Sodom shall be justified before you] (cf. Ezek 16:48; Lam 4:6). For the people of Sodom resisted angels, but this people attacked the Lord of all, the God of all and their King; they dared to kill the King of angels, and did not know that the Christ whom they killed lives to this day.

1.2.0.en: "The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider" [3].

1.2.1.en: If God called Israel His firstborn son (Ex 4:22), it was fitting for the son to know his Father, to perceive His mysteries, and to respond to His purposes and will; but through his disobedience man sank down to something lower than the dumb animals. As St. John Chrysostom says, man sank to something lower than the animal, so the Lord Christ took our nature and ascended into the heavens to raise our nature to what is heavenly.

1.2.2.en: Man has sunk so low that it is said in the Book of Proverbs: "Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise" (Prov 6:6).

1.2.3.en: The ox and the ass are known for their stupidity when compared with the rest of the animals, and yet, when they are hungry, they go by instinct to their master at the place of food, as though asking him to let them eat. But Israel, whose life was embittered by captivity, became hungry and naked, and yet did not return to God, its Father, who cares for it and attends to it. What the animals practice by instinct surpassed the conduct of rational man in his wickedness!

1.2.4.en: If man has sunk so low, below the animal, then the Word of God incarnate was born in a manger, so that when man draws near, as to the manger, he finds the Lord Christ as food for him. He eats, and his insight is opened to perceive the mysteries of God through his union with the only-begotten Son, who knows the mysteries of His Father, for He says: "neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whom the Son will reveal him" (Mt 11:27).

1.2.5.en: Here is a divine call addressed to us, whom the Lord Christ acquired by His blood, and whose souls He fed with His Body and Blood; therefore it is fitting for us to listen to His words and respond to His call.

1.2.6.en: St. John Chrysostom compares the Jews in the Old Testament with the believers in the New Testament with regard to the knowledge of God, saying that the former knew God in their thought but not in their life, experience and works (Tit 1:16).

1.2.7.en: * Their error is not in their (mental) ignorance but in their wickedness, in their evil will, for even when they knew it, they chose to be ignorant.

1.2.8.en: * Before the Cross even the Jews did not know (the Father), for it was said: "Israel doth not know," but after the Cross the whole world ran to Him.

1.2.9.en: St. John Chrysostom * Without doubt the mystery of the Kingdom of Heaven was hidden in the Old Testament, and it had to be revealed in the fullness of time in the New Testament. The Apostle says: "for they drank of that spiritual Rock that followed them: and that Rock was Christ" (1 Cor 10:4)... Christ Himself was symbolized to them by the rock, but to us He was declared in the flesh.

1.2.10.en: St. Augustine * How can you not consider it a terrifying thing, if those who know God (in the mind) did not recognize the Lord (at His coming), while the two stupid animals, the ox and the ass, know who feeds them, and Israel was found to be more stupid than they?!

1.2.11.en: St. Clement of Alexandria * They crowned Jesus and lifted Him up, bearing witness to their ignorance.

1.3.s.en: 4. A description of the people's condition:

1.3.0.en: 4 Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters! They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backward. 5 Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. 6 From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores: they have not been closed, neither bound up, neither mollified with ointment. 7 Your country is desolate, your cities are burned with fire: your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers. 8 And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city. 9 Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.

1.3.1.en: After summoning lifeless nature and the irrational animals to witness God's trial with man, He disclosed the condition to which the people had come, like a bill of indictment, which said:

1.3.2.en: First: He described them with seven traits in [4], as though He were saying with the prophet Amos: "For three transgressions of Judah, and for four... For three transgressions of Israel, and for four" (Amos 2:4, 6). The three signify the inner sins of the soul, which is in the image of the Trinity, and the four signify the outward sins of the body, which was taken from the earth (the four quarters of the world). It is as though the people had been defiled within and without, by hidden and visible sins, in body and spirit.

1.3.3.en: The first four traits here signify the visible bodily sins: "Woe to the sinful nation, a people laden with iniquity, a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters"; and the last three traits represent the inner sins: "They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backward."

1.3.4.en: In any case, the number 7 signifies "Completeness," as though their sins had reached the full measure.

1.3.5.en: It is observed that Isaiah is fond of the number 7, for he often presents 7 traits in setting out different matters.

1.3.6.en: The bill of indictment came declaring these sins, which are summarized as follows:

1.3.7.en: A. Collective sins: "Woe to the sinful nation" [4]. If the sin of Achan the son of Carmi caused destruction to the people (Josh 7:11), how much more if the whole nation turns aside to evil?! Corruption had crept into the priests as into the people, into the nobles as into the common folk, so there was need of a collective return to God, as the people of Nineveh did. This people was called "the holy nation," but it isolated itself from the Holy One and bore the trait "sinful nation," using the Hebrew word goi, an expression particular to the Gentiles because of their not clinging to God. It is as though this nation had turned aside from its purpose to enter the ranks of the nations foreign to God.

1.3.8.en: B. The weight of their iniquity: "a people laden with iniquity" [4]. Since the prophet Isaiah prophesies about the Savior and salvation, he had to bring out the weight of the sin under whose burden souls are bowed down... God alone knows the weight of this iniquity, for the Word of God came incarnate, the Lamb of God who taketh away the sin of the world (Jn 1:29, 36).

1.3.9.en: Under the weight of sin the soul is bowed down until it sinks as in the waters of the world, and so it bears the nature of the world, not of heaven. Therefore it is said of Pharaoh and his army: "they sank as lead in the mighty waters" (Ex 15:10), and it is said of wickedness: "and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof" (Zech 5:8).

1.3.10.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa sees that the man who walks in the virtuous life is light in weight spiritually, while the wicked man is heavy and sinks in the waters. Virtue is light and makes man like a cloud rising upward, and like a dove that flies on its small wings (Isa 9:8). Origen spoke at length about this, showing how Peter nearly drowned because of sin (doubt), and when the Lord gave him faith he walked on the waters.

1.3.11.en: C. Rooted in evil: "a seed of evildoers, children that are corrupters" [4]. Sin crept into the life of their forefathers, so the generations came rooted in evil from their fathers and grandfathers. As the Lord said to the scribes and Pharisees: "Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers. Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers" (Mt 23:32-33).

1.3.12.en: D. Their forsaking of the Lord, the source of holiness: "They have forsaken the LORD, they have despised the Holy One of Israel, they are gone away backward" [4]. There is nothing worse than for a man to forsake his God, the source of his life and the secret of his holiness. The Lord says through Jeremiah: "For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water" (Jer 2:13).

1.3.13.en: If Isaiah saw the holy God (Isa 6), He is the "Holy One of Israel," the source of the sanctification of His believers, granting us His traits working in us! The prophet repeated this expression 20 times.

1.4.0.en: E. An incurable disease: "Why should ye be stricken any more? ye will revolt more and more: the whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint. From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it; but wound and bruise, and a fresh stroke that has not been pressed nor softened with oil" [5-6].

1.4.1.en: By saying: "Why should ye be stricken any more?!" God declares that this people had rejected sonship to God, and therefore was no longer worthy to be the object of God's concern and discipline. He had already disciplined them as His sons, but they revolted more and more, so He wishes to stop the fatherly disciplines, leaving them to receive the fruit of their natural corruption, for He says: "My people would not hearken to my voice; and Israel would none of me. So I gave them up unto the hardness of their hearts, and they walked in their own counsels" (Ps 18:11-12). And it is written in Jeremiah: "Wherefore will ye plead with me?... In vain have I smitten your children; they received no correction" (Jer 2:30), "I have stricken them, but they have not grieved; I have consumed them, but they have refused to receive correction" (Jer 5:3).

1.4.2.en: Now God leaves them to their corruption, which they chose by their own will, so that disease creeps into their body from the head to the heart to the foot. It creeps into the mind so that they become unable to manage, and also into the heart so that their inner affections and feelings are defiled, and down to the feet from below so that they become unable to move toward God on the royal way of His Kingdom. Corruption crept into the leaders and great men (the head), as into the servants and priests (the heart), and into the common people (the body), even into the despised among them (the sole of the foot).

1.4.3.en: The wounds became deadly and the bleeding does not stop... There is no one who moves to rescue and save, and no one who offers the oil of love to soften the harsh stroke!

1.4.4.en: Corruption struck human nature itself, as St. Cyril of Jerusalem says:

1.4.5.en: [Great is the wound of human nature; from the foot to the head there is no soundness in it.]

1.5.0.en: F. Complete desolation: "Your country is desolate; your cities are burned with fire, your land, strangers devour it in your presence, and it is desolate, as overthrown by strangers. And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers, as a besieged city" [7-8].

1.5.1.en: The prophet speaks here of what would befall Judah after the invasion of Sennacherib the Assyrian, counting what would befall them in the future as though it were present, because it was bound to happen.

1.5.2.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem says: [Isaiah lived about 1000 years ago, and he saw Zion as a shelter (for cattle); the city at that time was standing and beautiful in its public benefits and clothed with greatness... But he says: "And the daughter of Zion is left as a cottage (a shelter for cattle) in a vineyard, as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers." Now we find the place full of cucumber planting. See how the Holy Spirit enlightens the saints.]

1.5.3.en: The land that flows with milk and honey, the Promised Land that God gave to His people, for whose sake the people endured walking in the wilderness for forty years, became desolate. Sennacherib seized 46 fortified cities, so Jerusalem was under direct threat of danger, "as a besieged city" and "as a lodge" or "cottage" that is easy to occupy... Its inhabitants saw what the strangers (the Assyrians) did to their cities, setting fire to them, and the fire consumed their produce before their eyes while they were unable to move. Their cities became desolate, as overthrown by strangers, that is, as Sodom and Gomorrah were overthrown before, or as if a violent flood of water had flooded over them and shattered them.

1.5.4.en: This desolation that came is a sign of the iniquities Judah had committed, and a natural necessity of their forsaking God their Sanctifier, their turning back from Him, and their not obeying His voice, for it was said: "But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the LORD thy God, to observe to do all his commandments... that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee: Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field" (Deut 28:15-16).

1.5.5.en: So every soul that does not cling to God its Sanctifier, desolation comes upon all its cities: upon body, soul, mind and heart with all the feelings and emotions, and so on... Every fortification is taken away from it, and it becomes like a cottage or a tent in the open, an easy prey in the hands of sin.

1.5.6.en: * These are those who defile themselves and turn them from being the house of the heavenly Father, the holy Jerusalem, the house of prayer, into a den of thieves... They take from it what is precious, and plunder from it the best it has so that it becomes as nothing.

1.5.7.en: Origen The expression "is left" of the daughter of Zion here points to the position of the people of God, whom He counted as His own people, the virgin daughter and the pampered bride, who has become forsaken, "left alone"; she feels isolation (Loneliness) and abandonment, and this is the harshest punishment upon a human soul! The daughter of Zion brought this punishment upon herself. She was a pampered bride and became abandoned and divorced. Origen says: [I think that the Husband (God) wrote a bill of divorce for His former bride, and gave it into her hand, and sent her out of His house.]

1.6.0.en: In the midst of this complete desolation God finds a small faithful remnant that bears witness to Him, for whose sake He did not destroy His corrupted people, for it was said: "Except the LORD of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah" [9]. The Apostle Paul quoted this statement in (Rom 9:29). It is as though what happened in the days of Isaiah is repeated in all generations, even in the apostolic age, when a faithful few of the Jews accepted faith in the Lord Christ.

1.6.1.en: God does not care for great numbers but for the small remnant that is sanctified to Him in the midst of the corruption that overtakes the many. This remnant is the "little flock" to whom it is the Father's good pleasure to give the Kingdom (Lk 12:1); this remnant the Lord of hosts left for Himself as His own work, granting it His Holy Spirit to sanctify it to Him, so that it becomes a holy leaven that leavens the whole lump.

1.6.2.en: * See that you belong to the chosen few, and do not walk in coldness imitating the slackness of many; live as the few, so that you may be made worthy with them to enjoy God, because many are called, but few are chosen (Mt 20:16).

1.6.3.en: St. John Cassian For the sake of this small remnant God shortens the days of tribulation, especially in the last times, for it is said: "but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened" (Mt 24:22).

1.7.0.en: "Hear the word of the LORD, ye judges of Sodom! Give ear unto the law of our God, ye people of Gomorrah:" [10].

1.7.1.en: With courage, without fear or flattery, Isaiah calls the judges of the people "judges of Sodom" and gives the people themselves the title "people of Gomorrah," because of the injustice and corruption that marked both the rulers and the ruled.

1.7.2.en: In the whole book we find not one situation in which the prophet feels fear or weakness except at his seeing the Lord Christ in His glory (Isa 6), for Isaiah fears God, not men.

1.7.3.en: He sees that the only cure for the judges, as for the people, is the word of the Lord and His Law.

1.8.0.en: 11 To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices unto me? saith the LORD: I am full of the burnt offerings of rams, and the fat of fed beasts; and I delight not in the blood of bullocks, or of lambs, or of he goats. 12 When ye come to appear before me, who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts? 13 Bring no more vain oblations; incense is an abomination unto me; the new moons and sabbaths, the calling of assemblies, I cannot away with; it is iniquity, even the solemn meeting. 14 Your new moons and your appointed feasts my soul hateth: they are a trouble unto me; I am weary to bear them. 15 And when ye spread forth your hands, I will hide mine eyes from you: yea, when ye make many prayers, I will not hear: your hands are full of blood.

1.8.1.en: The accusation directed at them here is extremely serious; for He did not ascribe to them atheism or the practice of idol worship, but ascribed to them hypocrisy; they practice the worship of God with great precision and with a deadly literalism; they offer many sacrifices and offerings and keep the feasts, while their hearts are far from God and their lives are corrupt.

1.8.2.en: This accusation is directed against those who profess faith throughout all generations, who keep the letter while ignoring the inner spirit, as it was said to the angel of the Church of the Laodiceans: "Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked" (Rev 3:17), because he imitated the Pharisee who said: "God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess" (Lk 18:11-12).

1.8.3.en: This accusation moved the Fathers of the Church to disclose the purpose of worship in the life of the Church, whether in the New Testament or the Old, and the obligation not to deviate from this divine purpose:

1.8.4.en: A. St. Irenaeus says: [God shows that He has no need of anything (Isa 1:11); He only urges them and counsels them to practice these things so that man may be justified and draw near to God.]

1.8.5.en: God wants us, through our worship, to draw near to Him and be united with Him so that we bear His nature in us, the nature of love and mercy. For He desires mercy, and not sacrifice (Hos 6:6; Mt 9:13). Therefore He rebukes the Jews, saying that they spread forth their hands for prayer with importunity but are not heard, because their hands are full of blood through committing murders (Isa 1:15); instead of love they bore hatred and the killing of souls and bodies, especially the killing of the prophets and those who spoke the word of truth.

1.8.6.en: * Why these divisions? Because we keep the feast but with the leaven of malice and wickedness, and so we divide the Church of God into parts, keeping what concerns its outward matters while excluding the better things: faith and love. We have heard from the prophetic words that such feasts and fasts do not please the Lord.

1.8.7.en: St. Irenaeus * It is clear to everyone that the piety that leads to worship and honor is the oldest and greatest of causes, and that the Law itself urges justice and teaches wisdom... by calling to the Creator of the world and its Father.

1.8.8.en: St. Clement of Alexandria B. They offered many sacrifices and burnt offerings in the temple of the Lord, and chose the fatlings, but God is not pleased with them, for He did not ask for the sacrifices in themselves, because He has no need of them, but asked for them as a symbol of the unique sacrifice of the Lord Christ, for the reconciliation of man with God and his enjoyment of fellowship with Him. But the goal was lost to them, for when Christ the Sacrifice came they rejected Him; they offered animal sacrifices and celebrated the feast of the Passover and denied the true Passover, the Lamb of God who taketh away the sin of the world.

1.8.9.en: * In the days of the Lord the Jews thought that they were celebrating the Passover, but they did this in vain because they persecuted the Lord. By their own testimony the Passover no longer bore the name of the Lord, for it was called the Passover of the Jews (Jn 6:4), not the Passover of the Lord... because they denied the Lord of the Passover.

1.8.10.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * All these (sacrifices) were abolished so that the new Law of our Lord Jesus Christ might be fulfilled, which He fulfills not under the yoke of obligation (but by His will, since He offered Himself as a ransom).

1.8.11.en: Epistle of Barnabas C. They used to gather to celebrate the weekly feasts (the sabbaths), the monthly and the yearly feasts, which the Lord counted as His own feasts, in which He was pleased because He gathers with His people and fills them with His divine joy.

1.8.12.en: These assemblies became a burden to God, and His soul hated them (Isa 1:14), so He no longer counts them as His assemblies.

1.8.13.en: * The Lord did not ascribe (these practices that they kept) to Himself but counted them as the works of sinners (since they are hateful to Him), whether the new moons or the sabbaths or the great day or the fasts or the feasts.

1.8.14.en: In the Law concerning the sabbath we read in the Book of Exodus: "... To morrow is the rest of the holy sabbath unto the LORD"... "Eat that to day; for to day is a sabbath unto the LORD" (Ex 16:23, 28).

1.8.15.en: Origen D. In more than one place God assures His people that when He brought them out of the land of bondage He did not give them laws concerning sacrifices (Isa 1:12), lest they think that He brought them out out of a need for their worship or their offerings; rather, that they themselves might enjoy Him... Pope Athanasius the Apostolic says that God wanted to draw them away from the idols and attract them to Himself, giving them the laws at the proper time (after their exodus); and yet they forgot God, who had worked wonders with them in Egypt, and went back to worshiping the calf (Ex 16:3). The laws concerning sacrifices came after they received the Law, so that they would not offer them to idols but to the true God. What was required of them was to learn first to abandon the idols and to care for God's commandments, and after that to offer sacrifices (Jer 7:22).

1.8.16.en: * He does not accept sacrifices from you, nor did He command you first to offer them out of need for them, but because of your sins.

1.9.0.en: St. Justin Martyr E. He says: "who hath required this at your hand, to tread my courts?!" [12]. They multiplied their entering into the temple to offer sacrifices without number, and God saw them, in their lack of repentance, as like the animals that trample His house and defile it! The offering of sacrifices turned from reconciliation with God into the pouring out of God's wrath.

1.9.1.en: They came with offerings like incense, which symbolizes prayer, but since they gave the Lord the back and not the face (Jer 2:27), their incense became an abomination to the Lord, because it carried the smell of their hypocrisy and their lack of repentance.

1.9.2.en: * Works that are done in a way contrary to the will of God, or that are offered without fitting reverence, profit nothing... God has no need of anything, since nothing makes Him unclean! He has reached the end because of their conduct, full of hypocrisy [11].

1.9.3.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * The Lord our God is not pleased with the keeping of such things; if there is found among you a man who breaks his oath, or a thief, let him cease from this; and if there is found an adulterer, let him repent; and then he keeps the sweet and true sabbaths of God. If anyone has unclean hands, let him wash and be purified.

1.10.0.en: 16 Wash you, make you clean; put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes; cease to do evil; 17 Learn to do well; seek the truth, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow. 18 Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool. 19 If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: 20 But if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.

1.10.1.en: God exposed them before themselves, showing the ugliness of the corruption that had come upon them, without crushing them with despair or wounding their souls; rather, with heavenly fatherly love He offered them the cure, to cover them and restore them to the good nature in which He had created them. This cure is repentance springing from faith and mingled with love, and its steps are:

1.10.2.en: A. Washing: by saying "Wash you" [16] He does not mean the ceremonial purifications of the Law, because in His accusation of them He asks that they not stop at the outward form of worship; rather, He means the washing of Baptism, in which we put off the old man in order to bear in us the new man who is in the image of our Creator. This is what the Lord meant by saying to the human soul: "Then washed I thee with water" (Ezek 16:9), as it is written in the same book: "Then will I sprinkle clean water upon you, and ye shall be clean: from all your filthiness... A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you" (Ezek 36:25-26).

1.10.3.en: In the Old Testament the priests could not enter the temple unless they first washed, or else they would die (Ex 30:19-21), and the Psalmist says: "I will wash mine hands in innocency: so will I compass thine altar, O LORD" (Ps 26:6). It is an inward washing! St. John Chrysostom says: [He does not mean the washing with water that the Jews practiced, but the washing of the conscience.]

1.10.4.en: "Make you clean" [16]. If by Baptism we received the new man, we received a new capacity to practice the new life in Christ, which is purity of heart, as a condition for seeing God, for the Lord says: "Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God" (Mt 5).

1.10.5.en: * As you enter the good font of great glory, run with reverence in the race of goodness. For the only-begotten Son of God is present here and ready to save you, saying: "Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest" (Mt 11:28). You have put on the coarse garment of your transgressions and have been bound with the ropes of your sins; now hear the word of the prophet: "Wash you, make you clean, and your sins shall be blotted out from before mine eyes," that the choir of angels may sing over you, saying: "Blessed is he whose transgression is forgiven, whose sin is covered" (Ps 32:1). You who light the lamps of faith, keep them in your hands unquenched.

1.10.6.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem * So if by the washing (in Baptism), as the prophet says, in that mystical font, our will is purified and evil is removed from our souls, then by this we become better people and reach a better state.

1.10.7.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa B. "Put away the evil of your doings from before mine eyes" [16]. When man receives the purity by which he sees God, he is able to distinguish the works of evil from the divine work, and so he rejects everything that is evil, so that he does not halt between the two ways: God and sin.

1.10.8.en: Our receiving the sacrament of washing and purification gives us a divine capacity for earnest work in discovering ourselves in the Lord, that we may enter into a continual washing (by repentance) and cleansing from everything of evil that belongs to our inner being... We confess our sins to God and so enjoy continual ascents toward Him until we see Him face to face.

1.10.9.en: * Behold, you see that it is in your power to deposit in your hearts either ascents, that is, thoughts that belong to God, or descents, that is, thoughts debased toward carnal and earthly things.

1.10.10.en: Abba Serenus We confess our sins and put away our evil, and so we see God in us declaring Himself and His glory within us. As St. Augustine says: [Show yourself to the One who knows you, and He will reveal Himself to you, who do not know Him.]

1.10.11.en: "Cease to do evil" [16]. If by true repentance we put away evil from the eyes of the Lord, then the sign of our sincerity toward Him is that we cease completely from every evil deed. This is a divine gift, but it is not granted without being asked for with faith and importunity, with striving and perseverance.

1.10.12.en: * He desires to give an opportunity for repentance to all His beloved, confirming it by His almighty will. Therefore let us obey His great and glorious will; and as we plead, asking for His mercy and the tenderness of His compassion, leaving every vain work and strife and envy that leads to death, let us return to Him and cast ourselves upon His mercies.

1.11.0.en: St. Clement of Rome C. "Learn to do well" [17]: the negative side is not enough, that is, removing everything that is evil and always ceasing from it; here there is an obligation to positive work, that we bear in us the trait of Christ who is "the Truth." We seek "the Truth," that is, we seek our living Christ dwelling in us and working through us, practicing the work of Christ, the Lover of mankind, who cares for the oppressed, the needy and the weak. Therefore He commands us: "seek the truth, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow." This is positive repentance, through which we return to God not merely to cease from evil and injustice but to stretch out our hands with practical love and mercy, especially toward the helpless and the widows.

1.11.1.en: * Would that we all, men and women, might stretch out our hands to them, so that we do not fall under the sorrows of widowhood. Let us care for them, and so prepare for ourselves a great storehouse of tenderness, for the tears of widows can open heaven itself. Would that we might not trample on them so that their misfortunes increase, but help them by every means.

1.11.2.en: St. John Chrysostom * See how everywhere God reckons works of great mercy, for they stand in favor of those who have erred.

1.12.0.en: St. John Chrysostom D. Practical love toward the suffering and needy is a natural reflection of our experience with God, who has compassion on us, who does not look down on us but asks for dialogue with Him as His friends. He opens the doors of His mercies before us sinners, saying: "Come now, and let us reason together, saith the LORD: though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool" [18].

1.12.1.en: This is a plain evangelical call, declaring God's longing for the salvation of every person who accepts fellowship with the Holy One through the Cross.

1.12.2.en: In His love, although God had confirmed the terrible judgment upon the sons of Judah, He quickly seeks reconciliation. He is not like man, who meets stubbornness with stubbornness and anger with anger, but pours soothing oil on the inflamed wounds, to bring every soul back to Him.

1.12.3.en: God asks man to enter into dialogue with Him, while we sometimes find some Christian emperors who closed the door before those who had sinned, and sometimes we even find shepherds, and even parents, who bear the same spirit that is foreign to the spirit of God, the Lover of mankind.

1.12.4.en: God wants to wash the blood of our sins (the scarlet and the crimson) with His pure blood, so that we become like snow in whiteness and like wool in purity (Song 8:5); we become His shining garment as at His transfiguration.

1.12.5.en: Some see that the word "let us reason together Cheyene" here means that we put an end to arguing, for God knows that man no longer has anything to say because of his sins, which have become visible like the scarlet color that cannot be wiped away; therefore He wished to bring him out of the predicament and open to him the door of divine pardon so as not to wound his feelings... a wonderful divine love!

1.12.6.en: By His call directed to us to reason together with Him, He asks us to judge ourselves by ourselves, for when we perceive our sins and confess them, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins (1 Jn 1:9). We judge ourselves, so that we are not judged.

1.12.7.en: * Let no one despair of himself, even if he has reached the extreme of evil, even if he has passed into the habit of doing evil, yes, even if he bears the very nature of evil, let him not fear... Great is the power of repentance, for it at least makes us like snow, we become white as wool, even if sin has ruled over us and dyed our souls.

1.12.8.en: St. John Chrysostom * He does not recall our evil deserts, but still has compassion on us and urges us to repentance.

1.12.9.en: * It is within God's authority alone to grant the forgiveness of sins and to accuse us of transgressions, since He commands us to forgive our repentant brothers every day, "and He will forgive us" (Mt 6:14).

1.13.0.en: St. Clement of Rome E. The sanctity of human freedom: God opens the doors of His love before all but compels no one, for He seeks the human heart as a voluntary offering; He presents the way to him and gives him the capacity to work, and at the same time leaves him the freedom to choose, for He says: "If ye be willing and obedient, ye shall eat the good of the land: but if ye refuse and rebel, ye shall be devoured with the sword: for the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it" [19-20].

1.13.1.en: * Behold, you see that we must first purify ourselves (that is, bear a holy will), and then God purifies us.

1.13.2.en: * We are masters; it is within our power to make every member in us an instrument of evil or an instrument of righteousness.

1.13.3.en: * Man can change suddenly and be turned from earthenware to gold. What concerns virtue and vice is not (compulsory) by nature, but can easily be changed... I know that everyone wishes to fly to heaven from now, but there is need to show the wish by action.

1.13.4.en: St. John Chrysostom * By saying this [19] He proves that acceptance or refusal depends on us.

1.13.5.en: St. Clement of Alexandria observes here that the steps of repentance mentioned in [16-17] are seven: two negative steps in verse 16 (washing and ceasing from evil) and five positive steps mentioned in verse 17, which must be practiced.

1.14.0.en: 21 How is the faithful city become an harlot! it was full of truth; justice lodged in it; but now murderers. 22 Thy silver is become dross, thy wine mixed with water: 23 Thy princes are rebellious, and companions of thieves: every one loveth gifts, and followeth after rewards: they judge not the fatherless, neither doth the cause of the widow come unto them.

1.14.1.en: Here he compares what Jerusalem was before with what she became through her deviation and corruption, in a style full of lament and deep sorrow. The prophet Isaiah is entirely frank, yet he is full of love and affection!

1.14.2.en: A. Jerusalem was the "faithful city" [21], and she became a "harlot." He likens her to the bride who was faithful to her heavenly Bridegroom, keeping His commandments and declaring His splendor and glory through her life, and who ran after another (idol worship) and was defiled by her spiritual adultery with her lovers (Ezek 16:25, 32, 36). She was a virgin (Isa 37) united with her Bridegroom, the Giver of holiness, but she left Him and united herself with abominations.

1.14.3.en: * You can say that God the Word left the synagogue of the Jews as an adulteress, parted from it, and took for Himself a wife of harlotry from the Gentiles, because those who were "Zion, the faithful city" became adulterers, while the others became like Rahab the harlot, who received the spies of Joshua and was saved, she and all her house (Josh 6:5).

1.14.4.en: Origen B. She was "full of truth; justice lodged in it; but now murderers" [21]. She was a dwelling for the Holy One, who is "the Truth" and "Justice"; the Lord lodged in her because He found His rest in her, but she became a dwelling for murderers, therefore the Lord says: "The Son of man hath not where to lay his head" (Mt 8:10; Lk 9:58). When she is holy she says: "My beloved is mine; he shall lodge betwixt my breasts" (Song 1:13); but when she is defiled, her heart "between her breasts" becomes a dwelling place of evil.

1.15.0.en: C. Falsehood crept into her, so her silver became dross, bearing the shine of silver and its appearance but not bearing the substance of silver or its value. Her wine became mixed with water [22], bearing the color of wine but adulterated with water... This is a picture of attention to the formalities of worship and the literal carrying out of the commandments in outward appearances, without attention to the depths. Our Christ turns water into wine, but the evil one turns wine into water.

1.15.1.en: Silver signifies the word of God (Ps 12:6), and wine signifies the joy of the Spirit. The formalist holds fast to the word of God, and perhaps keeps it by heart, but he does not bear Christ, "the Word of God," in his heart or in his conduct. He has the appearance of spiritual joy while being far removed from the joyful heavenly life and the fellowship of the angels and saints in the Lord.
